items.title: Incomplete tensor product of one-mode Hilbert spaces with a reference vector
items.statement: For a unit reference vector Ω in L²(R), the coherent isometric embeddings L²(Rⁿ)→L²(Rᵐ), f↦f⊗Ω^{⊗(m−n)}, define an incomplete tensor product by Hilbert completion; each one-coordinate rank-one projection P_j^Φ for a unit Φ is well-defined and orthogonal.
items.strategy: Verify the embeddings are coherent isometries by Fubini, define the compatible union, then show the coordinate projection formulas are contractions compatible with the embeddings.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is assumed for the Hilbert completion; the finite-coordinate isometries and local projection calculations use no choices.

items.title: Heisenberg group polarization and the fixed-central-character orbit
items.statement: In symplectic coordinates the Heisenberg group is a topological semidirect product of an abelian normal subgroup N=R^n×R by a Lagrangian R^n; for every nonzero central parameter λ, the corresponding K-action on the characters of N with central character t↦e^{iλt} is free and transitive.
items.strategy: Verify the cocycle and semidirect multiplication directly, then compute the dual action on coordinate characters.

items.title: The universal Weyl norm is finite and has the C*-completion property
items.statement: The symplectic phase is a normalized 2-cocycle, the twisted finite-support algebra has the stated involution, and its supremum over cyclic *-representations is a finite nonzero C*-seminorm whose quotient completion is universal for unitary Weyl generators.
items.strategy: Prove the cocycle identity, construct algebraic GNS representations of positive states, bound every representation by the ℓ¹ coefficient norm, and complete the quotient.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used only in the Cauchy-sequence completions of the algebraic GNS spaces and the C*-normed quotient; the finite algebraic identities and coefficient-state witness are choice-free.

items.title: The Schrödinger Weyl system is regular and irreducible
items.statement: For n≥0 and λ≠0, the operators on L²(R^n), (Sλ(q,p,z)f)(x)=e^{iλz+iλp·(x−q/2)}f(x−q), form a strongly continuous irreducible unitary representation of the stated Heisenberg group; its Weyl operators satisfy the fixed phase convention.
items.strategy: Check the multiplication law and strong continuity directly; prove irreducibility by Fourier uniqueness and Tonelli’s theorem.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used only through L² translation continuity and L¹ Fourier inversion; the phase calculation and Tonelli contradiction are choice-free.

items.title: The Gaussian Weyl average is a rank-one projection
items.statement: For every a>0 in the one-mode Schrödinger system, the weak Gaussian Weyl average (2π)⁻¹∫exp(−aq²/4−p²/(4a))W(q,p)dqdp is the orthogonal projection onto Ωₐ(x)=(a/π)¹/⁴exp(−ax²/2), whose Weyl orbit is total; intertwiners commute with the average, and on incomplete tensor products it is the local coordinate projection.
items.strategy: Compute the integral kernel by the Gaussian Fourier transform, then use Fourier uniqueness to prove totality.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited only from the L¹ Fourier inversion supplier; the Gaussian integral calculation is choice-free.

items.title: Stone–von Neumann uniqueness for finite-dimensional regular Weyl systems
items.statement: Assume AC. For a finite-dimensional real symplectic space (V,ω) and real λ≠0, every nonzero irreducible regular Weyl system with W(v)W(w)=e^(−iλω(v,w)/2)W(v+w) is unitarily equivalent to the Schrödinger system on L²(R^n); the latter is irreducible, so the equivalence class exists and is unique.
items.strategy: Convert the Weyl system to a Heisenberg-group representation, use the spectral measure of its abelian normal subgroup to obtain a transitive system on the fixed-central-character orbit, and apply Mackey imprimitivity with trivial stabilizer.
items.axiom_use: AC is required by the published spectral-measure, transitive-system, and Mackey-imprimitivity suppliers. The countable dense sets and conull intersections below are explicitly indexed by rational coordinates and a fixed countable dense subset, so they require no additional choice. The separately cited Schrödinger-model lemma has its own Countable Choice dependency.

items.title: At zero central parameter, distinct regular characters are inequivalent
items.statement: On the standard symplectic plane at λ=0, every real-linear character defines a regular irreducible one-dimensional Weyl system; the characters ℓ₀(q,p)=0 and ℓ₁(q,p)=πq are inequivalent.
